City of Ann Arbor
                                          Proposal A
 Charter Amendment Tax for Street, Bridge, and Sidewalk Repair and Replacement
Shall the Charter be amended to authorize a new tax up to 2.125 mills for street and bridge
repair and for sidewalk repair and construction for 2027 through 2032 to replace the
previously authorized tax up to 2.125 mills for street and bridge repair and for sidewalk
repair and construction for 2022 through 2026, which will raise in the first year of levy the
 estimated revenue of $19,236,316? In accordance with State law, a portion of the millage
may be subject to capture by the Ann Arbor Downtown Development Authority and the
Washtenaw County Brownfield Redevelopment Authority.

 Amendment to Modify the Method for Counting Signatures of Nomination Petitions
Shall Section 13.9 of the City Charter be amended to specify that if an individual signs
multiple candidates' nomination petitions for a single elected office, only the earliest-dated
signature shall count, and that if two or more signatures bear the same date, none of those
signatures shall count? Currently, if an individual signs multiple candidates' nomination
petitions for a single office, every signature of that individual is disregarded, regardless of
date.

excerpt:
Augusta Charter Township
                    Fire Protection and Prevention Millage Increase
Shall the previous authorized increase in the tax limitation imposed under Article IX, Sec. 6,
of the Michigan Constitution in Augusta Charter Township, of 2.0 mills ($2.00 per $1000 of
taxable value), be increased in an additional amount of up to 1 mill ($1.00 per $1,000 of
taxable value) for a total of up to 3 mills ($3.00 per $1,000 of taxable value) and levied for
four (4) years, 2027 through 2030 inclusive, on all taxable property within Augusta Charter
Township, Washtenaw County, Michigan, for the purpose of providing fire protection and
prevention services in the Township, including but not limited to adding duty crews and
being able to replace outdated equipment? This 1 mill increase will raise an estimated
$396,610 in the first year the millage is levied.

excerpt:
Northfield Township
                   Fire Service and Medical Rescue Millage Proposal
This proposal will allow the Township to levy 2.5 mills (reduced to 2.4206 due to Headlee)
to fund. fire service and medical rescue in Northfield Township for 5 years beginning
December 2027, annually adjusted downward due to the Headlee Amendment.

Shall the limitation on the amount of taxes which may be imposed on taxable property
within Northfield Township, County of Washtenaw, Michigan, be collected in an amount
not to exceed 2.5 mills ($2.50 on each $1,000.00 of taxable value), for a period of 5 years,
beginning with the 2027 Winter tax bill and ending with the 2031 Winter tax bill, inclusive,
as a renewal of the current millage (2.4206 mills due to Headlee rollback from 2.5) which
expires after the 2026 Winter tax collection, to provide funds for fire services and medical
rescue including operations, staffing, equipment purchase, and maintenance?
It is estimated that 2.5 mills would raise approximately $ 1,339,796.7 when first levied in
December 2027.

       Scio Township Road, Bridge, and Culvert Improvement Millage Proposal
Shall the limitation on the amount of taxes which may be imposed each year for all
purposes on real and personal property in Scio Township, Washtenaw County, Michigan,
be increased as provided in Section 6, Article IX of the Michigan Constitution by the levy
0.5 mills ($0.50 per $1,000 of taxable value) for a period of six (6) years, beginning with the
December 1, 2027 tax levy and continuing through 2032 inclusive, for the purpose of
providing dedicated township funding to be used to leverage other sources including
private, Washtenaw County, or the state of Michigan, for the maintenance, repair,
preservation, reconstruction, and improvement of local public roads as certified by Michigan
Department of Transportation, bridges, bike lanes, crosswalks, and culverts within the
Township, including related engineering, inspections, drainage, and administrative costs?
This millage is estimated to raise approximately $984,536.00 in the first year the millage is
levied.

Clinton Community Schools
                           Operating Millage Renewal Proposal
This proposal will allow the school district to continue to levy the statutory rate of not to
exceed 18 mills on all property, except principal residence and other property exempted by
law, required for the school district to receive its revenue per pupil foundation allowance
and renews millage that will expire with the 2026 tax levy.
Shall the currently authorized millage rate limitation of 18.487 mills ($18.487 on each
$1,000 of taxable valuation) on the amount of taxes which may be assessed against all
property, except principal residence and other property exempted by law, in Clinton
Community Schools, Lenawee and Washtenaw Counties, Michigan, be renewed for a
period of 6 years, 2027 to 2032, inclusive, to provide funds for operating purposes; the
estimate of the revenue the school district will collect if the millage is approved and 18 mills
are levied in 2027 is approximately $1,580,000 (this is a renewal of millage that will expire
with the 2026 tax levy)?
